newsitem.title: INDIA: Anti-Miss World rally stays peaceful after suicide.
newsitem.headline: Anti-Miss World rally stays peaceful after suicide.

text.p: The Miss World show will go on in India despite the suicide of a man who set himself ablaze in protest against the beauty pageant, organisers said on Friday.
In Bangalore, the south Indian city where Miss World will be crowned on November 23, a 1,000 strong demonstration against the beauty contest coming to India passed off peacefully.
The 89 beauty queen contestants awoke in their hotel guarded by around 100 policemen inside and another 100 outside.
Later, they went by bus for a rehearsal at the Chinnaswamy cricket stadium, the venue for the final night, flanked by jeeps of armed police who accompany them everywhere in Bangalore.

Elsewhere in the city, protesters chanted "Down with Miss World," echoing words uttered by Suresh Kumar on Thursday before he lit his kerosene soaked clothes in Madurai, a city 432 kilometres (270 miles) south in neighbouring Tamil Nadhu state.
Kumar's next and last words, according to local reports, were "water, water, water".
By the time onlookers doused the flames he had 90 percent burns.
"We are very saddened by what has happened but the show will go on," Sanjiv Gupta, chief executive officer of Amitabh Bachchan Corp Ltd, the organisers of the event, told Reuters.
Right-wing Hindu nationalist party leaders who led the march made no mention of Kumar, an unemployed member of an extremist marxist group, in speeches at the end of the rally.
"My party workers should come from every corner of Karnataka to lay siege to the stadium," Anant Kumar, a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) member of parliement, exhorted the crowd.
Earlier, the police had banned rallies involving more than 10 people, but apparently compromised on an orderly demonstration.
India's famous "Bandit Queen", Phoolan Devi, now a member of parliament after 11 years in jail, also supported the pageant and said the BJP was politicising the event.
"What's wrong if the beauty is presented beautifully with Indian touch and style?" the Press Trust of India news agency quoted her as saying.
So far, a series of events held in the run up to the final night have passed off smoothly, but have been cloaked in a blanket of security.
But Kumar's apparent martydom has heightened the state of alert in the Bangalore police.

Even before Kumar took his life, the Mahila Jagran Samiti (Forum for Awakening Women) threatened its members would join the audience on the final night and take cyanide to lessen the pain before committing self-immolation.
The activist Farmers' Association has also threatened to torch the stadium on the night of the final.
"We are on guard. It may have repercussions here," G.K. Bekal, Bangalore deputy police commissioner in charge of security for the show, told Reuters.

Security plans suffered a setback on Friday when a judge deferred his decision on whether to allow the state government to call in crack paramilitary teams to back up 12,000 local police already deployed.

Opponents of Miss World say the pageant, which raises around $150 million for charity and drew a global television audience of up to two billion last year, degrades women and represents a "cultural invasion".
But polls conducted by a national newspaper have shown little groundswell support for the militants.
In a sop to the opposition, the swimsuit section of the contest was held outside India, in the Seychelle Islands, last weekend.
